pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR will transparently take ownership of any client-side-apply fields when `--server-side` apply is used. If this is not done, then it will not be possible to remove fields previously used by client-side-apply with server-side-apply (without manually patching managed fields yourself).

Previously this change was [proposed in a KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3518), but during discussion with the SIG we have [scoped it down to a bug fix](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3518#discussion_r984724392).

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->

addresses issues brought up in the following and likely more bug reports

Fixes #107980
Fixes #108081
Fixes #107417
Fixes #112826
Fixed #99003

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
For `kubectl`, `--server-side` now migrates ownership of all fields used by client-side-apply to the specified `--fieldmanager`. This prevents fields previously specified using kubectl from being able to live outside of server-side-apply's management and become undeleteable.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

<!--
This section can be blank if this pull request does not require a release note.

When adding links which point to resources within git repositories, like
KEPs or supporting documentation, please reference a specific commit and avoid
linking directly to the master branch. This ensures that links reference a
specific point in time, rather than a document that may change over time.

See here for guidance on getting permanent links to files: https://help.github.com/en/articles/getting-permanent-links-to-files

Please use the following format for linking documentation:
- [KEP]: <link>
- [Usage]: <link>
- [Other doc]: <link>
-->
```docs
- [Discussion]: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3518#discussion_r984724392
```

/sig cli
/cc @soltysh @KnVerey @apelisse

issue_context.title: Object (/v1, Kind=Endpoints: test-endpoint) keeps changing, diffing without lock
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

When diffing an `Endpoints` object with `--server-side=true`, there is no diff produced, but this message is printed:

```
W0207 05:09:34.901634   96076 diff.go:692] Object (/v1, Kind=Endpoints: test-endpoint) keeps changing, diffing without lock
Error from server (Conflict): Apply failed with 1 conflict: conflict with "kubectl-client-side-apply" using v1: .subsets
```

A diff without `--server-side=true` yields empty output as expected

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected there to be simply no diff. A client-side diff reports no changes, as expected.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

test.yml: 
```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Endpoints
metadata:
  labels:
    tanka.dev/environment: 85d1b5ffe5bfdd8a4aae0983528822b49fd733dbe02b7d09
  name: test-endpoint
  namespace: apps
subsets:
- addresses:
  - ip: 192.168.178.2
  ports:
  - port: 9999
```

```
kubectl apply -f test.yml
kubectl diff -f test.yml --server-side=true
```

### Anything else we need to know?

If the `test.yml` gets **applied** via `--server-side=true`, there is no error, but the `time` field changes, so this is undesirable in my case.

The yaml is generated via tanka 0.20, but I double-checked the output against Kubernetes documentation, and it seems perfectly valid.

If I remember correctly this was working back when I was using `minikube` version `1.20.0` (with whichever Kubernetes version was the default of that). I was also using tanka with that, and the same `Endpoins` config.

### Kubernetes version

<details>
```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"23", GitVersion:"v1.23.3", GitCommit:"816c97ab8cff8a1c72eccca1026f7820e93e0d25", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2022-01-25T21:17:57Z", GoVersion:"go1.17.6", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/arm64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"22", GitVersion:"v1.22.6+k3s1", GitCommit:"3228d9cb9a4727d48f60de4f1ab472f7c50df904", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2022-01-25T01:27:44Z", GoVersion:"go1.16.10", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```
</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>

</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
```

comments: What is the reason to use `diff` with `server-side=true`, even if you already applied using `client-side`?. I understand the reason using `client-side` because of `time` field, however, maybe it'd be better also use diff command with client-side.

Yeah, there are a few things that I don't understand here. 

What is the problem you're concerned about:
1. the poor interaction between client-side and server-side?
2. The warning about "keeps changing, diffing without lock"?
3. The time change?

> What is the reason to use diff with server-side=true, even if you already applied using client-side?

@ardaguclu This is what tanka does internally to compare the local state (rendered as yaml) with the k8s API. This works on every other object, except for `Endpoints`-Objects. And this worked in a previous version of Kubernetes, so I believe this is a regression.

> Yeah, there are a few things that I don't understand here.
> 
> What is the problem you're concerned about:
> 
> 1. the poor interaction between client-side and server-side?
> 2. The warning about "keeps changing, diffing without lock"?
> 3. The time change?

@apelisse I would expect a `kubectl diff -f test.yml --server-side=true` to properly diff the change, instead of erroring out. It does so for every other Object. My comments about an apply with `server-side=true` were just to illustrate the fact, that in that case, the diffing of the `subsets` field works fine if the resource was created with that flag.

This has worked before and stopped working somewhere between minikube 1.20 (I believe this was kubernetes 1.21 or 1.20) and Kubernetes 1.22.6.

I don't know how the internals work, but I would guess, that something goes wrong when diffing the `subsets` array, which causes it to not be a stable comparison.
I don't know how this would have worked before 1.20, did we have server-side apply at that time? For sure we know that client-side and server-side integration aren't great.

👋  Not sure if this would be helpful, but I had a pre 1.20 minikube and kubectl version and I just tested this:

```bash
➜  bin git:(206bcadf021) ✗ ./kubectl version
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"19+", GitVersion:"v1.19.1-dirty", GitCommit:"206bcadf021e76c27513500ca24182692aabd17e", GitTreeState:"dirty", BuildDate:"2022-02-14T16:29:35Z", GoVersion:"go1.17.6", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/amd64"}

➜  bin git:(206bcadf021) ✗ ./kubectl apply -f ~/test.yml
endpoints/test-endpoint configured
```

Thanks for testing this @jcleira . I might be misremembering then, so it is definitely not a regression. Sorry for that confusion.

Regardless, I would still assume the diff to not fail at this point :)

I got to have a look more in detail on the diff command under `--server-side=true`.

Using the flag is triggering an `apply` attempt for the endpoint BEFORE doing the `diff`, and the conflict is the error returned because the initial `apply` is a client-side apply and the second one (triggered by adding the flag as mentioned) is `server-side`.

It would work with this command chain:
```bash
kubectl apply -f test.yaml --server-side=true
kubectl diff -f test.yml --server-side=true
```

Probably we could inverse the order and do the `diff` then the `apply`, so the error message would be something like:

```bash
diff -u -N /var/folders/y_/sv0954yd5cb51y9l2w8v8c840000gn/T/LIVE-2264261010/v1.Endpoints.default.test-endpoint /var/folders/y_/sv0954yd5cb51y9l2w8v8c840000gn/T/MERGED-1608721413/v1.Endpoints.default.test-endpoint
--- /var/folders/y_/sv0954yd5cb51y9l2w8v8c840000gn/T/LIVE-2264261010/v1.Endpoints.default.test-endpoint	2022-03-01 17:34:52.000000000 +0100
+++ /var/folders/y_/sv0954yd5cb51y9l2w8v8c840000gn/T/MERGED-1608721413/v1.Endpoints.default.test-endpoint	2022-03-01 17:34:52.000000000 +0100
@@ -14,7 +14,7 @@
       f:subsets: {}
     manager: kubectl
     operation: Apply
-    time: "2022-03-01T16:34:40Z"
+    time: "2022-03-01T16:34:52Z"
   name: test-endpoint
   namespace: default
   resourceVersion: "31703"
W0301 17:21:36.876011   92434 diff.go:692] Object (/v1, Kind=Endpoints: test-endpoint) keeps changing, diffing without lock
Error from server (Conflict): Apply failed with 1 conflict: conflict with "kubectl-client-side-apply" using v1: .subsets
```

I do understand the perspective of these comments, i.e. that they're going to re-apply again later anyway, but if they are using kubectl in a CI system, they may well not see the warning and encounter problems from the bug in the intervening period.

EDIT: a potentially relevant precedent to consider is what SSA does when it successfully applies but fails to sync the CSA annotation [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5078091aa5b82bd1de32d209a489645d50713705/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/fieldmanager/lastappliedupdater.go#L61-L68). Is it worth mentioning _why_ we want to keep it even though the user is on SSA? I.e. that it is required for downgrade to be possible (per the [docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/server-side-apply/#downgrading-from-server-side-apply-to-client-side-apply) and the [KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90187))

Should we also sanity check in the loop below that each result actually matches the operation provided?

For this one, I'm wondering if we should also skip if the _current_ field manager name isn't `kubectl`. The current behaviour always preserves the annotation because it continues to be owned by the CSA manager, BUT the downgrade doesn't actually work, because the annotation is not being kept in sync. So it would be a behaviour change... but arguably the retention when it is not kept correct is a bug. Wdyt?

To be clear, this is a suggestion to drop the annotation if during the migration the user is not using the default `kubectl` field manager? I am on board but want to be clear that this entails the annotation gets dropped if the field manager is not `kubectl` at the time of the first migration.

> want to be clear that this entails the annotation gets dropped if the field manager is not kubectl at the time of the first migration.

Yes, that's what I'd expect. Can you think of any reason it would be valuable to retain in that case? The docs explicitly say that custom field managers opt out of the downgrade capability. Imagining the following sequence:
1. `kubectl apply -f mycm.yaml`
2. `kubectl apply -f mycm.yaml --server-side --field-manager=custom`
3. `kubectl apply -f mycm.yaml`

If step 2 made any changes, step 3 is going to use broken logic whether or not we keep the annotation, because the data it is using is either empty (behaves like a fresh apply) or stale (behaviour undefined).  I guess if they instead do:

1. `kubectl apply -f mycm.yaml`
2. `kubectl apply -f mycm.yaml --server-side --field-manager=custom`
3. `kubectl apply -f mycm.yaml --server-side --force-conflicts`
4. `kubectl apply -f mycm.yaml`

Then step 3 will repair the annotation if it is still present? I guess that could be considered useful, but I don't like the tradeoff of essentially undefined behaviour (instead of "this behaves like a fresh apply") in the first workflow, which I feel would be more common.

(fwiw I don't think my other argument re: users relying on it for miscellaneous reasons applies here, because for one thing they are actively opting in, and for another, invalid data is at best useless and at worst harmful.)

>  Can you think of any reason it would be valuable to retain in that case?

One consideration is that in the current form if an applier made use of the the `kubectl` field manager later, the annotation would be updated once again. But yeah you are right that at that point even the updated annotation would have dubious contents since it would be missing fields from the custom field manager.

> Then step 3 will repair the annotation if it is still present? 

Step 2 would have caused the annotation to be dropped since it would have no owner. It would be gone by no. 3.

> One consideration is that in the current form if an applier made use of the the kubectl field manager later, the annotation would be updated once again.

If they really want that, would it work for them to add the annotation in with a blank value themselves? Experimentally, it seems to (create an object with SSA and then add `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration: "{}"` to it--suddenly it will be populated!)

> Step 2 would have caused the annotation to be dropped since it would have no owner. It would be gone by no. 3.

If we don't opt it out of our migration process here, then the special field manager would be keeping it around in 2 and 3, no?

1. `kubectl apply -f mycm.yaml`
2. `kubectl apply -f mycm.yaml --server-side --field-manager=custom`
3. `kubectl apply -f mycm.yaml --server-side --force-conflicts`
4. `kubectl apply -f mycm.yaml`

(fwiw I don't think my other argument re: users relying on it for miscellaneous reasons applies here, because for one thing they are actively opting in, and for another, invalid data is at best useless and at worst harmful.)
